source: arXiv:2510.09333v2 Table 1 (IHQ-unscr., Top-1 accuracy); Sec. 4 protocol

data.note: the public HF release is smaller than the numbers in Appendix D Table 6; exact replication of the paper's sample is therefore impossible

protocol.gt: top item of the full IHQ-all fit (paper's fallback gt; official CLIC 2024 leaderboard not available)

mutation.description: each pair's winner re-drawn by a fair coin (rater signal destroyed), 100 bootstraps

notes: NOT reproduced, neither in magnitude nor in ordering: we measure BBQ=44.20%, Crowd-BT=71.40%, Bayes-BT=23.20% -- our Crowd-BT reimplementation is the most stable top-1 identifier, the opposite of the claim. Confounders that make this a NON-refutation: (a) the public IHQ release has 1,921 comparisons / 59 raters vs 2,062 / 62 in Appendix D Table 6; (b) the official CLIC 2024 leaderboard used as gt is not redistributed, so we used the paper's fallback gt (full-data fit; all three models agree the top item is the uncompressed 'reference'); (c) Crowd-BT is our own SGD reimplementation, not the Google implementation the paper benchmarked, and its stability is hyperparameter-dependent (lr=0.02, 20 epochs); (d) 500 bootstraps vs 10,000. Only the Crowd-BT > Bayes-BT ordering reproduces. The task spec quotes 61.92/33.15/24.32 while arXiv v2 Table 1 prints 61.42/32.44/23.59.
